correctness.rationale: On the dual ell_infinity^n, p-admissibility is columnwise sum_k |u_kj|^p<=1. With row maxima r_k=max_j|u_kj|, sum_k r_k^p<=n; for finite q, v_k=r_k^(p/q-1)u_k is q-admissible because |u_kj|<=r_k. Positive homogeneity and Hölder give ||f||_p<=n^(1/p-1/q)||f||_q for every lattice polynomial; q=infinity follows directly. h_n(u)=max_j|u_j| has ||h_n||_r=n^(1/r) exactly, from column constraints and coordinate row witnesses, establishing equality. Equivalence of norms on dense free vector lattice extends identity to onto isomorphism; norm one holds on generators. For infinite I the same finite-support witnesses force nonbounded-below injective dense inclusion, hence proper nonclosed range; order continuity fails by the published Theorem 5.1 equivalence. Zero-row, n=1, q=infinity and all real p boundaries checked; independent rescaling computations corroborated p,q=(1,2),(1,3),(2,4),(1,9).

value.rationale: Exact sharp quantitative comparison constant for natural free Banach lattice scale over coordinate ell_1^n and an infinite-dimensional dichotomy. Distinguishes the ell_1 case from published Hilbert-space p<q<=2 behavior. It is a motivated, all-dimension exact norm fact, not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice.

final_claim: For real 1<=p<q<=infinity and n>=1, the canonical generator-preserving map J:FBL^(p)[ell_1^n] -> FBL^(q)[ell_1^n] is onto, has norm 1 and exact inverse norm n^(1/p-1/q), attained by the maximum of absolute coordinate evaluation generators. For every infinite index set I, the analogous map on ell_1(I) has dense nonclosed proper range and is not order continuous for all p<q.
limitations: All free Banach lattices real, with standard convexity-one free p norm; exact constant only for ell_1^n and infinite ell_1(I), not arbitrary Banach generators.
